name: 识别主题
scenario: a transport notice
chunks: The main point of this notice is that the schedule has changed.
If I had to summarise this in one sentence, it is about service disruption.
The key information is in the first two paragraphs.
Everything else is just background or explanation.
patterns: The main point is that ___.
If I had to summarise: ___.
dialogue: What is this transport notice about?
The main point is that the schedule has changed. Weekend services will be replaced by buses for the next three months.
That is a big disruption. Is there more detail?
The key information is in the first two paragraphs. Everything else is just background about why the work is needed.
So the bottom line is: no trains on weekends, use replacement buses.
Exactly. That is the thirty-second version.

name: 提取关键信息
scenario: a workplace announcement
focus: Pulling out who, what, when, and where
chunks: The key details are: the office will close at three on Friday, and all staff should work remotely.
Let me pull out the essential information: who is affected, what is changing, and when.
The announcement has three main points worth noting.
The rest of the message is context, not new information.
patterns: The key details are: ___.
Let me pull out: who ___, what ___, when ___.
dialogue: Can you extract the key information from this workplace announcement?
The key details are: the office will close at three on Friday for maintenance, and all staff should work remotely after that.
Everyone on the third and fourth floors. The first and second floors are not affected. The announcement has three main points, but the rest is context.

name: 区分主次
scenario: a lengthy policy document
chunks: The primary change is the new deadline policy. The rest is just explanation.
If you only remember one thing, it should be the submission deadline.
I have highlighted the essential parts. The supporting details are in the appendix.
Not everything in this document carries equal weight.
patterns: The primary change is ___.
If you only remember one thing: ___.
dialogue: Emma, this policy document is twenty pages. What is the primary change?
The primary change is the new deadline policy. Everything else explains why and how. If you only remember one thing: submissions after the fifteenth will not be processed until the following month.
Got it. I will focus on that and refer to the appendix only if I need more detail.

name: 一句话概括
scenario: a research summary
focus: Condensing information into one clear sentence
chunks: In short, the study found that remote workers are more productive but less collaborative.
If I had to capture the essence, it is about the productivity-collaboration trade-off.
The bottom line is that the investment paid off within six months.
That is the thirty-second version of a much longer story.
patterns: In short, ___.
The bottom line is ___.
dialogue: Can you give me a one-sentence summary of this research?
In short, the study found that remote workers are more productive but less collaborative. The bottom line is that companies need a hybrid model to get the best of both.
That is helpful. Is that really the core finding?
Yes. The other thirty pages are methodology and detailed breakdowns by industry.

name: 识别事实
scenario: a product review
chunks: The statement about battery life is a fact because it can be tested.
This is a factual claim: the device weighs 1.2 kilograms.
A fact can be proven true or false, regardless of who says it.
The first part of the review is factual; the second part is opinion.
patterns: This is a factual claim: ___.
A fact can be ___, regardless of ___.
dialogue: Is the claim about battery life in this review a fact or an opinion?
The statement that the battery lasts eight hours is a fact because it can be tested. Anyone can run the same test and get the same result.
What about the claim that it is the best phone on the market?
That is clearly an opinion. A fact can be proven true or false. Best is subjective.

name: 识别评价
scenario: a restaurant review
chunks: When the reviewer says the food is the best in the city, that is clearly an opinion.
Words like disappointing and amazing signal subjective judgment, not fact.
This part is the writer's personal reaction, not an objective claim.
An opinion cannot be proven wrong, but it can be poorly supported.
patterns: When ___ says ___, that is an opinion.
Words like ___ and ___ signal subjective judgment.
dialogue: This restaurant review calls the food the best in the city. Fact or opinion?
Clearly an opinion. Words like best, amazing, and disappointing signal subjective judgment. An opinion cannot be proven wrong, but it can be poorly supported.
So how do I know if it is a useful review?
Look for specific, verifiable details. The reviewer mentions the pasta was undercooked—that is closer to a factual observation.

name: 识别推测
scenario: a news article about economic trends
chunks: The article uses words like may and could, which signal speculation, not established fact.
When a journalist writes that the economy is expected to grow, that is a forecast.
I notice the author hedges a lot in the second half of the article.
There is a difference between what the data shows and what the writer thinks it means.
patterns: Words like ___ and ___ signal speculation.
There is a difference between what ___ shows and what ___ thinks.
dialogue: This economic article uses is expected to a lot. What does that tell you?
It signals speculation, not certainty. Words like may, could, and is expected to are hedging language. The data shows one thing, but what the writer thinks it means is different.
So should I trust the predictions?
Treat them as informed guesses, not facts. The author hedges more in the second half, which is where the real uncertainty is.

name: 说明证据
scenario: a health claim in an online post
focus: Evaluating whether a claim is backed by evidence
chunks: The post makes a strong claim, but it cites no source. That is a red flag.
A claim without evidence is just an assertion.
The study they reference is from 2006 and only included thirty participants.
The evidence provided is too weak to support such a broad claim.
patterns: The claim is ___, but it cites no source.
The evidence is too ___ to support ___.
dialogue: This post claims a certain food prevents illness, but cites no source. What do you think?
The post makes a strong claim with no evidence. That is a red flag. A claim without evidence is just an assertion.
The study is from 2006 and only included thirty participants. The evidence is too weak to support such a broad claim. I would not share this.

name: 询问来源
scenario: a forwarded message with alarming news
chunks: Before I react, where did this information originally come from?
Do we know who wrote this and when?
The message does not say who the original author is. That worries me.
A credible source should be identifiable and verifiable.
patterns: Where did this information originally come from?
A credible source should be ___.
dialogue: Lin, I got this alarming forwarded message. Should I be worried?
Before you react, where did this information originally come from? Do we know who wrote this and when?
I am not sure. It was forwarded three times.
The message does not say who the original author is. A credible source should be identifiable. Let us check before acting on it.

name: 检查时间背景
scenario: an old statistic being shared as new
chunks: This data is from 2019. A lot has changed since then.
The information may have been accurate at the time, but it is now out of date.
Before we use this statistic, we need to check if there is more recent data.
Old information presented without a date can be misleading.
patterns: This data is from ___. A lot has changed since then.
Before we use this, we need to check ___.
dialogue: This statistic is being shared everywhere, but it is from five years ago.
Then a lot has changed since then. The information may have been accurate at the time, but it is out of date. Before we use it, we need more recent data.
People are treating it as current.
Old information without a date is misleading. We should find the latest figures before we repeat this.

name: 对比两个说法
scenario: two conflicting reports about the same event
focus: Comparing sources for agreement and contradiction
chunks: One report says fifty people attended, and the other says two hundred. That is a significant discrepancy.
Both sources agree on the main event, but they differ on the details.
When two credible sources conflict, the safest response is to reserve judgment.
The areas where they agree are more reliable than where they differ.
patterns: One says ___, the other says ___.
When sources conflict, the safest response is ___.
dialogue: Two reports about the same event give very different attendance numbers. How do you reconcile them?
One says fifty attended, the other says two hundred. That is a significant discrepancy. Both agree the event happened, but differ on scale.
When credible sources conflict, reserve judgment. The areas where they agree—that the event occurred—are more reliable than disputed numbers.

name: 保留判断
scenario: an unverified rumour at work
chunks: I am not going to form an opinion until I see more evidence.
Let us treat this as unverified for now.
It is possible the rumour is true, but it is equally possible it is not.
The responsible thing is to wait for confirmation before acting.
patterns: I am not going to form an opinion until ___.
Let us treat this as ___ for now.
dialogue: Mia, there is a rumour about layoffs. I am not going to form an opinion until I see official confirmation.
It is possible, but equally possible it is not. Let us treat this as unverified. The responsible thing is to wait for facts before we act on it.

name: 转述原话
scenario: what the manager said in the briefing
chunks: She said, and I quote, the deadline will not be extended.
Her exact words were that the project is on hold pending review.
I want to be careful to represent what she actually said, not my interpretation.
According to her, the changes will take effect next month.
patterns: She said, and I quote, "___".
According to ___, ___.
dialogue: What exactly did the manager say about the deadline?
She said, and I quote, the deadline will not be extended under any circumstances. Her exact words. I want to be careful to represent what she said, not my take on it.
According to her, the changes take effect next month. That part was less definitive, but the deadline was firm.

name: 概括他人观点
scenario: summarising a colleague's proposal
chunks: To summarise Ben's position: he supports the change but wants a phased approach.
The key point she was making is that timing matters more than budget.
If I understand correctly, his main argument is about cost efficiency.
I want to make sure I am representing her view accurately.
patterns: To summarise ___'s position: ___.
The key point ___ was making is ___.
dialogue: Can you summarise Mia's proposal? I missed part of the discussion.
To summarise Mia's position: she supports the change but wants a phased approach over six months. The key point she was making is that timing matters more than the budget.
Yes. She thinks a phased approach reduces the risk of disruption. I want to make sure I am representing her view accurately—she was quite specific about the timeline.

name: 调整细节量
scenario: explaining a technical issue to a non-technical colleague
focus: Adapting detail level to the listener
chunks: For the executive summary, I will keep it high-level. For the technical team, I will include specifics.
Let me give you the short version first, and we can go deeper if needed.
The amount of detail you need depends on what you will do with the information.
I can go into more depth on any part you are curious about.
patterns: For ___, I will keep it high-level. For ___, I will include specifics.
Let me give you the short version: ___.
dialogue: Ben, do you want the high-level version or the technical details on the server issue?
The short version: a configuration error caused the server to restart during peak hours. It is fixed now and we added monitoring to prevent it.
That is enough for me. Thanks.
I can go into more depth if you need it—the technical team has the full incident report.

name: 说明不确定性
scenario: reporting preliminary findings
focus: Communicating what is known and what is unclear
chunks: The preliminary results suggest a positive trend, but the sample size is small.
We are reasonably confident about the first finding, but the second is uncertain.
It is important to note what we do not know yet.
I would treat these numbers as indicative rather than definitive.
patterns: The preliminary results suggest ___, but ___.
We are confident about ___, but ___ is still uncertain.
dialogue: How confident are you in these preliminary findings?
The results suggest a positive trend, but the sample size is small. We are reasonably confident about the first finding. The second is still uncertain.
I would treat them as indicative, not definitive. Note what we do not know yet. The full analysis will be ready next week.

name: 概括短报道
scenario: a news article about a local policy change
chunks: The article reports that the city council voted to extend public library hours.
The headline focuses on the cost, but the article itself is more balanced.
The key change is that libraries will now be open on Sundays.
The reporter includes perspectives from both supporters and critics.
patterns: The article reports that ___.
The key change is that ___.
dialogue: Can you summarise this article about the library hours change?
The article reports that the city council voted to extend public library hours. The key change is that libraries will now be open on Sundays.
The headline focuses on the cost, but the reporter includes both supporters and critics. It is actually fairly balanced.

name: 解释影响
scenario: a report on rising housing costs
focus: Explaining why a news story matters
chunks: This matters because rising housing costs affect everyone, not just renters.
The most significant impact will be on students and young professionals.
If this trend continues, we could see families leaving the city.
The report has implications for local businesses as well.
patterns: This matters because ___.
If this trend continues, ___.
dialogue: Why does this report on housing costs matter to people like us?
This matters because rising costs affect everyone, not just renters. The most significant impact will be on students and young professionals.
If this trend continues, families could leave the city. That has knock-on effects for local businesses and schools too.

name: 回应不同解读
scenario: a controversial editorial
chunks: I can see why someone might read this differently.
The editorial makes a valid point about funding, even if I disagree with its conclusion.
Another way to interpret this data is that the policy is working but slowly.
Reasonable people can look at the same facts and reach different conclusions.
patterns: I can see why someone might ___.
Another way to interpret this is ___.
dialogue: You and Ben interpreted this editorial very differently. Can you see his perspective?
I can see why someone might read it that way. The editorial makes a valid point about funding. Another way to interpret the data is that the policy is working, but slowly.
So you are not saying he is wrong?
No. Reasonable people can look at the same facts and reach different conclusions. His focus on funding is legitimate.

name: 总结可信部分
scenario: a viral social media thread with mixed claims
chunks: Of the five claims in this thread, only two are backed by verifiable sources.
The core event probably happened, but many of the details appear exaggerated.
I would trust the parts that multiple independent sources confirm.
The responsible summary is: something happened, but the specifics are disputed.
patterns: Of the claims, only ___ are backed by verifiable sources.
The responsible summary is: ___.
dialogue: This viral thread makes several claims. What parts can we actually trust?
Of the five claims, only two are backed by verifiable sources. The core event probably happened, but many details appear exaggerated.
So do I share any of it?
I would trust only the parts confirmed by multiple independent sources. The responsible summary is: something happened, but the specifics are disputed.
